title: Top Camping Tents for Weekend Trips (2026)
summary: The North Face Wawona 6 is our top camping tent for families and groups, with the Kelty Wireless 6 for value and the Mountain Hardwear Mineral King 3 for couples.
method: Picks come from CleverHiker's camping tent guide (updated Oct 9, 2026, from a team that has tested more than 50 tents) and Outdoor Life's camping tent guide (May 8, 2026). Both name the North Face Wawona their best overall and both recommend the Kelty Daydreamer for dark sleeping and the NEMO Aurora Highrise.
assumptions: Prices change often. CleverHiker's listed prices are quoted below, so check the current price. Weights and sizes are CleverHiker's measurements for the sizes it tested. Capacity numbers are maximums, so CleverHiker and Outdoor Life both advise sizing up. We left out the REI Westward 6, REI Base Camp 6, REI Half Dome 3 and Marmot Tungsten 4 to keep the list short.

products.name: The North Face Wawona 6
why: Both CleverHiker and Outdoor Life name it the best camping tent overall. CleverHiker rates it 4.8 out of 5 and says it beats any other large shelter in its tests on space, durable materials, ventilation and its enormous front vestibule.

Outdoor Life's tester found it spacious for a family of three, with excellent head height and a vestibule big enough to leave a camp chair set up inside. It uses DAC poles and carries a limited lifetime warranty.
specs: Six-person, 116 x 94 x 76 in., measured weight 19 lb 7.1 oz
75.7 sq ft floor and a 76-inch peak
CleverHiker lists $585; check the current price
cons: Fully set up, it may not fit a tent pad
products.best_for: Families and gear-heavy groups who want a true basecamp
products.skip_if: You want something light or cheap

products.name: Kelty Wireless 6
why: CleverHiker's best bang for your buck, giving families more usable space for the money than almost anything else in its guide. The 86.5 sq ft floor and 74-inch peak give a family of four room to spread out.
Two vestibules keep shoes and gear out of the sleeping area, pre-attached guylines stash in pockets, and the carry bag makes packing painless for a bulky tent.
specs: Six-person, 118 x 106 x 74 in., measured weight 18 lb 15.4 oz
Feels roomy for 4 and tight for 5
CleverHiker lists $280; check the current price
cons: Can feel warm in still weather
products.best_for: Families who want tall, roomy camping without premium prices
products.skip_if: You carry your tent far from the car

products.name: NEMO Aurora Highrise 4
why: CleverHiker calls it a premium small-family tent with real standing height without a huge footprint, praising its fabrics, poles, zippers and quick setup, which it says one person can manage. Outdoor Life also lists the Aurora Highrise as a great camping tent with a lifetime warranty.
Steep walls and a 75-inch peak give a bright, open interior, and a large front door makes loading mattresses and gear easy.
specs: Four-person, 100 x 90 x 75 in., measured weight 15 lb 14 oz
Feels roomy for 3 and tight for 4
CleverHiker lists $400; check the current price
cons: Outdoor Life says it only comes in blue, which washes out colors inside
products.best_for: Couples and families of three who want a durable tent they can stand up in

products.name: Mountain Hardwear Mineral King 3
why: CleverHiker's favorite for one or two campers who want more portability than a family tent. At under eight pounds it is easy to move and split between two people, with large doors, dual vestibules and an efficient floor plan.
The all-mesh canopy gives excellent airflow and open views, and the fly can roll back for stargazing. The trade-off is standing height, since the 48-inch peak suits sitting but not walking around.
specs: Three-person, 90 x 68 x 48 in., measured weight 7 lb 13.7 oz
Feels roomy for 2 and tight for 3
CleverHiker lists $400; check the current price
products.best_for: Couples and solo campers who want light, easy weekend camping
products.skip_if: You want to stand up or sleep a family of four

products.name: Kelty Daydreamer 6
why: Both guides recommend it for light-sensitive sleepers. Outdoor Life's testers said fully enclosed it is pitch black in the middle of the day, and the kids in that tent were the last to wake.
CleverHiker says its Twilight Tech fly meaningfully darkens the interior, and the 120 x 107 inch floor and 77-inch center height give adults room to stand.
specs: Six-person, 120 x 107 x 77 in., measured weight 19 lb 12 oz
CleverHiker lists $270; check the current price
cons: Poor ventilation with the fly on
products.best_for: Families with kids or light-sensitive sleepers, mostly in fair weather
products.skip_if: You camp in hot weather or want long-term durability

products.name: Coleman Skydome 4
why: CleverHiker's best budget tent for casual campers and the simplest way into its guide. Integrated poles stay attached to the tent body, which removes much of the sorting that makes a first setup frustrating.
Two people get a roomy interior and three can fit, with a large door and a full-coverage fly on the tested version. Outdoor Life also finds Coleman tents run slightly small for their claimed size.
specs: Four-person, 96 x 84 x 56 in., measured weight 13 lb 11.2 oz
CleverHiker lists $190; check the current price
cons: Poor ventilation with the fly on
products.skip_if: You camp often or in rough weather

tips.title: How to choose
items: Outdoor Life says a 4-person tent only just fits four sleeping pads, so choose a 6-person tent if you need real space for four people.
CleverHiker says it matters most if you will spend time awake inside. Tall tents catch more wind, while low tents are steadier and lighter.
Look for a full-coverage fly in rain.
CleverHiker says full flies protect better in long rain while partial flies improve warm-weather airflow.
Budget for stakes and a footprint.
Several tents here do not include enough stakes or a footprint, so add what is missing before the trip.

faq: What is the best camping tent overall?
Both CleverHiker and Outdoor Life name The North Face Wawona their best overall camping tent.
What is the best cheap camping tent?
CleverHiker's best bang for your buck is the Kelty Wireless 6, listed at $280, and its best budget tent for casual campers is the Coleman Skydome 4, listed at $190.
Which tent is best for a couple?
CleverHiker picks the Mountain Hardwear Mineral King 3 for two campers, though its ceiling is low.
Which tent is best for kids who need darkness?
The Kelty Daydreamer 6 is recommended by both guides for blocking light, but it ventilates poorly with the fly on.
